subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO follow-up + customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>, Jill Harper <jill.harper@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO follow-up + customer-led load test coordination

Hi Samir / Jill 
Great to speak earlier 
- thanks for walking us through your production traffic pattern and the use cases you’re planning to migrate to Redwood. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps for the customer-led load test: 

Recap / SLOs discussed:
- Latency target: p95 <= 150 ms for typical request (no large context).
- Throughput target: sustained 200 req/s for the test window, with short bursts to 400 req/s.
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent clients; we'll validate scaling behavior up to 100 concurrent to be safe.
- Streaming: you have streaming partial-results requirement for the assistant UI (token streaming / chunked responses).
- Auth & data: test traffic will use masked data and a dedicated test account / API key.

Customer-led load test items we need from FinWise: 
1) Preferred 3-hour test window(s) (your proposed: July 7, 09:00–12:00 PT).
2) IP allowlist for the test runner(s) (we will provide IPs from our side for any inbound callback endpoints).
3) Test API key request (we will issue a scoped test key once ops confirms).
4) k6/Locust script — attached is our k6 starter script (k6_script_v1.js). Please review and sync any traffic shaping you want.
5) Test dataset notes and maximum context length we should use (please confirm masked payload sizes).

Attachments: k6_script_v1.js, mutual_action_plan.xlsx, redwood-tests-account-instructions.pdf

Next steps / owners: 
- FinWise: confirm test window and provide IPs + masked sample payloads (Samir / Jill) — due EOD Wed June 23.
- Redwood: provision scoped test API key and provide allowlist IPs and short runbook (Marissa / Aditya).
- Redwood infra: confirm runtime config for streaming and concurrency limits (Logan).

If that looks right I'll open a HubSpot activity and attach the mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

On Sun, 20 Jun 2027 at 15:05 Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com> wrote:
> Thanks — looking forward to the call.

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>, Jill Harper <jill.harper@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO follow-up + customer-led load test coordination

Quick internal note (looping in ops):

Marissa — I've reviewed the targets. From an infra perspective: 
- We can support p95 <= 150 ms for the typical path on the dedicated test pool if we pin to a 8-GPU cluster for the run. We'll need a 24-hour advance to reserve capacity for the July 7 window.
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked token streaming over SSE/WebSocket; for load testing k6 we typically simulate the streaming endpoints with chunked responses in the script. The k6 starter script has a comment about simulating streaming by polling; if they want true SSE from k6 we can provide a small harness.
- IPs: test harness will need to connect to our control endpoint for metrics; I'll provide a CIDR list by EOD tomorrow.
- Test API key: Aditya, can you provision a scoped key (test-only, limited quota) for FinWise and put instructions in the attached PDF?

I'll also add a short checklist for graceful degradation scenarios (fallback to smaller model variant) so that their test can exercise failover paths.

—
Logan
Lead SRE, Redwood

From: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Harper <jill.harper@finwise.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO follow-up + customer-led load test coordination

Thanks Marissa / Logan — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the window: 

1) Window: July 7 09:00–12:00 PT works for us. Can you also confirm a backup window July 9 same time?
2) Concurrency/Throughput: we want to validate up to 150 concurrent clients and sustained 300 req/s (our production bursts can reach this). Is the 8-GPU cluster still fine for that?
3) Streaming: our frontend needs real token-by-token streaming; polling won't be a realistic test. If you can provide an SSE/WebSocket harness or a small proxy we can run in our k6 worker that will accept the SSE stream, that'd be ideal.
4) IPs: ops@finwise will share the runner IPs (we use a k6 cloud runner and some on-prem workers).
5) Sample payloads: attaching two masked samples — one for short prompts and one for large-context (10k token masked). Please confirm whether the 10k context is realistic for the test or if we should constrain to 4k.

Attachments: (masked_payload_short.json, masked_payload_large.json)

If you can provision the test API key and allowlist by June 25 we can confirm and schedule the window.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform, FinWise

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finwise.com>, Jill Harper <jill.harper@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & SLO follow-up + customer-led load test coordination

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Samir. Quick responses / actions: 

1) Windows: We'll hold July 7 as primary and July 9 as backup. Noted.
2) Concurrency/Throughput: Logan — can you confirm whether the 8-GPU reservation covers sustained 300 req/s and up to 150 concurrent? If not, propose the smallest bump and estimated cost for a one-time test run.
3) Streaming: Aditya will attach a small SSE proxy we can include in the k6 workers so the frontend receives true streaming during the test. Aditya — can you also add a short example in the k6 script for wiring to the proxy?
4) IPs & API key: Aditya will provision a scoped test API key and share allowlist IPs for FinWise by EOD Fri June 25. \n5) Payloads / context: We can support up to 10k masked context for the test but recommend doing a tiered test (4k then 10k) so we can isolate performance delta.

I'll update the mutual action plan in HubSpot and send the DocuSign for the standard load-test terms (brief waiver + indemnity). If anything changes on your side, please flag.

Thanks!
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0147
